clue.text: Person developing long tooth cut short by hostile type

indicators.note: by means next to, so the shortened tooth sits beside the enemy

parts.note: a hostile type is an enemy, a foe

indicators.note: cut short says the word for tooth loses its final letter

parts.note: a long tooth, as on an elephant or walrus, is a tusk

explanation.surface: Someone growing long in the tooth gets cut down to size by an aggressive opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person developing' reads like someone maturing, but it is an unborn child developing in the womb; 'cut short' drops the K of TUSK.
explanation.definitionFit: An unborn offspring in the later stages of growth in the womb is a person still developing.

clue.text: See 23
Keen soldier on the front line?

indicators.note: on in this down clue places the soldier after, beneath, the front-line word

parts.note: on a First World War front line, troops occupied a trench
a soldier is a kind of ant, the caste that defends the colony

explanation.surface: An eager infantryman serving on the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier is the insect caste, not a person; the soldier ant placed on the trench gives the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means incisive or cutting, so a keen mind or keen criticism is trenchant.

clue.text: Very slight opportunity for a drink in heaven

indicators.note: in places the drinking spot inside the word for heaven

parts.note: the heavens are the sky
an inn is a place offering the chance of a drink

explanation.surface: There is only a tiny chance of getting a drink in paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny describes something very thin or slight, as in a skinny frame.

clue.text: High jumper has to move wearily, holding rocky line

indicators.note: holding means the plodding word contains the rocky ridge

parts.note: to trog is to walk wearily, to trudge
a reef is a ridge or line of rock near the surface of the sea

explanation.surface: A champion high jumper has to trudge along while carrying a line of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High jumper' suggests an athlete; it is a climbing amphibian. TROG is informal British for trudge.
explanation.definitionFit: This amphibian lives in trees and leaps from branch to branch, a jumper up high.

clue.text: Fate condemns the extraordinary work of Darwin

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests the letters of the first three words are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: Fate condemns the remarkable writings of Darwin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' looks like praise of the work but signals rearranging FATE CONDEMNS THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin published his book on human evolution under this title in 1871.

clue.text: Coverage, or lack of it?

definitions.meaning: being without cover or shelter, open to the elements

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both media publicity and the state of being unprotected from the weather.

clue.text: Quick run ending in wicket

parts.note: to run away is to flee

indicators.note: ending in picks out the final letter of the word wicket

explanation.surface: A fast single brings the end of the innings at the wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface (a quick run, a wicket) misleads: 'run' means escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet is a literary word for swift or fast-moving, as in fleet of foot.

clue.text: Dining elsewhere on nuts?

definitions.meaning: away from one's desk having a midday meal
crazy, not all there, an informal idiom

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means away eating lunch and idiomatically means crazy or out of touch.

clue.text: Invite me back after, say, food 22 21

annotationWithheld.why: Invite me back after, say, food 22 21 (8): the only parse reads 'Invite' as IN (container indicator) plus VITE (the container's letters), one clue word doing two jobs; EG and EM go in VITE
annotationWithheld.clue: Invite me back after, say, food 22 21

clue.text: Quite alluring

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adverb meaning fairly and as an adjective meaning attractive.

clue.text: Reformation grasping at art no more?

indicators.note: grasping means the reformation word holds the next word inside it

parts.note: a reformation of character is a conversion
taken as written

explanation.surface: A religious Reformation that clutches at art which no longer exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformation' tempts towards the Protestant Reformation; it just means a change of heart. The definition plays on the lament that talk is a lost art.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking together was once called an art, and people often complain it has died out.

clue.text: Nasty cut also for indicating non-runner

indicators.note: nasty suggests the following words are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A vicious cut to a horse also indicates it will not race.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing surface (non-runner) misleads: it is fabric whose dye will not run in the wash.
explanation.definitionFit: A dye or fabric that keeps its colour in washing does not run, so the label says it is a non-runner.

clue.text: Painter unknown in Asian holiday destination

indicators.note: in puts the unknown letter inside the destination

parts.note: Goa is a beach state in western India
y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An artist of uncertain identity turns up in an Asian resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the Spanish painter of The Third of May 1808.

clue.text: D-d-dog?

parts.note: the stammered word shows three initial Ds, so read it as a dog with three heads, the guardian hound of the classical underworld

explanation.walkthrough: The stutter is not a speech joke: the three Ds are three heads on one dog.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the three-headed hound guarding Hades bore this name, a dog with three heads.

clue.text: Extremely popular companion supporting English completely

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means the following pieces sit beneath the abbreviation

parts.note: extremely means very
in means fashionable or popular
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A very popular companion backs an Englishman to the hilt.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'supporting English' puts VERY IN CH below E.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in every respect, wholly, as in every inch a gentleman.

clue.text: Reduce size, getting private rooms into solid shape

indicators.note: into means the rooms go inside the solid shape

parts.note: a cone is a three-dimensional geometric solid
dens are small private rooms for retreat

explanation.surface: Downsizing by fitting private rooms into a solid shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to make something more compact, shrinking its volume or length.

clue.text: Having cut back course, one's afraid

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
Troon is a championship golf course on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: Having pruned the route back, somebody is scared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is not a route but the Scottish golf course TROON; 'one's afraid' means one who is afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: A poltroon is an utter coward, someone who is afraid.

clue.text: Score, with tip removed from setter's cue?

indicators.note: with tip removed means the first letter is taken off the command word

parts.note: a setter is a gun dog, and fetch is the command given to a dog

explanation.surface: A scoreline, with the tip taken off the crossword setter's prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the dog breed, not the crossword compiler; its cue is the command FETCH, which loses its F.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to scratch or engrave lines on it, which is to etch.

clue.text: Grim, beset by considerable smells

indicators.note: beset by means the grim word is surrounded by the size word

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a considerable size
dour means grim and stern

explanation.surface: Gloomy surroundings beset by powerful stenches.
explanation.definitionFit: Odours are scents or smells, often unpleasant ones.

clue.text: Earth god writhing in grass time and time again?

parts.note: earth is the ground

indicators.note: in puts the twisted letters inside the dried grass

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: writhing suggests the letters of god twist about

explanation.surface: An earth deity squirming in the grass, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth god' reads as a deity, but splits into the ground and a jumbled GOD. The definition alludes to the 1993 film in which one day repeats endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: From the 1993 film, the phrase names a day or situation that keeps repeating itself.

clue.text: See 22
Sister, half deaf, entering wrong word for Australia

indicators.note: entering means the sister and the half word go inside the jumbled word
wrong suggests the letters of word are put in the wrong order

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

indicators.note: half takes the first two letters of the word deaf

explanation.surface: A partly deaf sister keeps using the wrong word for Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes DOWR from WORD; NUN and DE (half of DEAF) enter it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a widely used informal nickname for Australia and New Zealand, lying below the equator.

clue.text: Miss extra, then no runs

parts.note: a miss is an unmarried girl, a maiden
something extra is left over

explanation.surface: Missing an extra, then scoring nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, and one off which no runs are scored is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket over bowled without a run being scored is given this name.

clue.text: Miss, female, follows vessel into open space

indicators.note: into means the vessel and the female letter go inside the open land

parts.note: a moor is open uncultivated land

indicators.note: follows means the female letter comes after the vessel

parts.note: an urn is a vase or vessel

explanation.surface: A young woman trails a vessel out into open country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a woman's title, as it did in the previous clue; here it is a verb, to pine for.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss someone is to grieve or long for them in their absence.

clue.text: Fish has egg on, by the way

indicators.note: by means next to, so the encouraging phrase sits beside the street

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to egg someone on is to urge them on

explanation.surface: A fish with roe on it, by the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests caviar, the egg of this very fish; 'egg on' is a verb meaning encourage.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish whose roe is caviar.

clue.text: Old poser's bit of leg captivating copper and rated sexy

indicators.note: captivating means the bit of leg holds the copper inside

parts.note: the shin is the front part of the lower leg
a penny, P, is a copper coin
an X certificate was a film rating for adult content

explanation.surface: An ageing model's leg, captivating a policeman and rated sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poser' suggests a vain model; the Sphinx posed riddles. 'copper' is a coin, not a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Sphinx of Thebes famously posed a riddle to travellers, an old setter of puzzles.
